recipes.name: Recursive asset-scene-task co-evolution
recipes.summary: Assemble scenes from assets, write tasks against what the scene actually contains, and let a feasibility critic reject the pairs whose goal cannot be reached, turning each rejection into a targeted scene edit.
recipes.background: Treat environment construction as a closed loop rather than a one-way pipeline: assets are generated first, scenes are assembled from assets, tasks are written against the scene, and each stage feeds failure information back to the one before it. Scene generation looks ahead to what the tasks will require, and task generation requests targeted edits to the scene when the task turns out to be infeasible, so scenes and tasks improve one another across rounds. Feasibility is enforced by a critic that inspects the assembled instance together with its task and rejects silently broken ones - the dominant failure mode is not an ugly scene but a scene whose target cannot be reached, which makes the task fail before it starts. Each round leaves two artifacts behind: the validated instance set and the edit log that explains what the loop learned.
recipes.produces: One scene and task pair whose goal state is reachable, passes the feasibility check, and admits a reference solution that succeeds in it.
when_to_use: the source separates raw material (assets) from the situations assembled on top of it
naively assembled scenes make many tasks infeasible, so a feasibility critic is needed
scene and task difficulty should co-evolve instead of being tuned by hand
not_when_to_use: the source provides one fully specified scenario with no generation freedom
there is no way to inspect an instance and decide whether it is feasible
inputs: an asset inventory or generator for the raw material
a scene assembler that composes assets into situated instances
a feasibility critic able to inspect an assembled instance together with a task proposal

steps.title: Generate the asset pool with queryable metadata
steps.detail: Produce or curate the raw material together with the attributes the tasks will reference, and record them as metadata so the scene and task stages query it instead of re-reading the source.
steps.accept: Every asset carries the attributes the tasks will reference, recorded as metadata the scene and task stages query.

steps.title: Assemble scenes from the asset pool
steps.detail: Compose assets into situated instances with context-aware placement, so the instance is coherent with the intent the tasks will ask about rather than a random arrangement.
steps.accept: The assembled instance places assets with context-aware placement and is coherent with the intent the task will ask about.

steps.title: Generate tasks against the assembled scene
steps.detail: Write instructions that operate on the scene's actual contents and specify the goal state precisely enough to be checked mechanically.
steps.accept: The instruction operates on the scene's actual contents and names a goal state precisely enough to check mechanically.

steps.title: Run the feasibility critic on the pair
steps.detail: Have the critic inspect the scene together with the task and reject instances where the goal is unreachable or the scene contradicts the instruction; this check is what stops silent failure from propagating into the dataset.
steps.accept: The critic rejects a planted instance whose target cannot be reached, and every retained pair passes the check.

steps.title: Convert failures into targeted edits
steps.detail: When an instance is rejected, turn the failure into a concrete edit request - move this asset, add that context, change this parameter - and apply it instead of regenerating from scratch, so the rejection is not wasted.
steps.accept: Each rejected instance has one concrete edit request recorded - move this asset, add that context, change this parameter - that was applied instead of a regeneration.

steps.title: Let scene generation anticipate downstream requirements
steps.detail: Start scene generation from the requirements the rejected task exposed, so the scene already satisfies the constraints the task generator keeps asking for, rather than hitting the same rejection again.
steps.accept: The scene is regenerated from the requirements the rejection exposed, and the reworked pair passes the feasibility check.

curation_notes: Run the loop over the whole set until the fraction of instances surviving the critic stops improving, and report the acceptance rate per round so the plateau is visible.
Keep the edit log alongside the corpus: it is the record of what each rejection taught the loop.
verifier: the critic rejects a planted infeasible instance whose target cannot be reached
the acceptance rate per round is reported and stops improving at the end of the run
every retained instance passes the feasibility check and admits a reference solution that succeeds in it
the edit log records a distinct targeted edit for each rejected instance
pitfalls: a lenient critic lets unreachable targets into the corpus, where they surface as task failures instead of generation failures
regenerating from scratch discards the information the rejection carried
assets without metadata cannot be queried by the scene or task stages, so the coupling is lost

source_papers.title: EmbodiedSmith: Scaling Embodied Data through Recursive Self-Improvement Flywheel in Simulation
source_papers.note: unifies asset, scene and task generation in an agentic refinement loop where scene generation anticipates downstream task requirements and task generation guides targeted scene edits

source_papers.title: V-CAGE: Vision-Closed-Loop Agentic Generation Engine for Robotic Manipulation
source_papers.note: closed-loop visual verification acts as a critic that filters silent failures and severs the error-propagation chain, with functional metadata backing the check

source_papers.title: ABot-ER: Unified Embodied Reasoning through Agentic Data-Model Co-Evolution
source_papers.note: agentic data-model self-evolution engine that continuously adapts the data strategy to the model's evolving capability state rather than fixing it in advance

recipes.name: Constraint-driven instance generation with validity gates
recipes.summary: Compile a constraint spec into a cost matrix and a deterministic expansion procedure, place assets by relation-driven geometry, and gate each instance on collisions, bounds, constraint violations and reachability.
recipes.background: Turn a compact specification of structural constraints into a family of concrete, valid instances, and gate every instance with an executable checker before it enters the corpus. The specification is compiled rather than paraphrased: a cost matrix derived from the stated constraints guides a deterministic expansion procedure - a graph search over a tile library, or a hierarchical sampler that places assets inside named functional zones - and each proposal is then compiled into geometry, with the relations extracted from the proposal driving fitting and local pose correction. The gates are the ones physics would impose: no collisions between placed elements, nothing outside the bounds, no violated constraint, and the task-relevant target reachable through the instance's own connectivity. Because the generator is parameterized by the constraint set, the corpus covers structural variation the source never showed explicitly, and every instance is reproducible from its seed and parameter values.
recipes.produces: One reproducible instance, rebuildable from its seed and parameter set, that passes the collision, bounds, constraint and reachability gates.
when_to_use: the source describes a family of environments that vary structurally rather than in content
many instances are needed and hand-authoring them does not scale
the validity of an instance is mechanically decidable (no overlap, in bounds, reachable)
not_when_to_use: the source is a single fixed artifact with no structural variation to model
the elements have no well-defined relation structure, so a relation-driven compiler cannot be written
inputs: a constraint specification (topology, zone layout, connectivity, scale or texture rules)
an asset or tile library the generator instantiates
a structural checker that decides validity of a produced instance

steps.title: Compile the constraint spec into a cost matrix
steps.detail: Turn each stated constraint into a cost or prohibition between structural elements, so the constraints become weights the generator optimizes rather than prose it must remember to respect.
steps.accept: Each stated constraint appears as a cost or prohibition between structural elements, with no constraint left as prose.

steps.title: Choose the expansion procedure
steps.detail: Use a deterministic search over the asset library (a graph traversal whose ordering the cost matrix guides) when the variation is structural, and a hierarchical sampler that proposes arrangements inside named functional zones when the variation is spatial.
steps.accept: The procedure is fixed for this instance: a cost-guided graph traversal for structural variation, or a hierarchical sampler over named functional zones for spatial variation.

steps.title: Extract relations and compile them into concrete placements
steps.detail: From each proposal extract the relations it asserts (containment, adjacency, orientation) and compile them into geometry via fitting and local pose correction; the compiler, not the proposal, is what makes an instance valid.
steps.accept: Each proposal's relations are compiled into geometry by fitting and local pose correction, and the compiled instance is what is checked.

steps.title: Run the validity gates
steps.detail: Reject any instance with an intersection between placed elements, any element out of bounds, or any element violating a stated constraint; write the gates as an executable checker so the corpus can be regenerated and re-audited at any time.
steps.accept: The executable checker reports zero collisions, zero out-of-bounds elements and zero constraint violations for the instance.

steps.title: Check reachability of the task-relevant state
steps.detail: Verify from the instance's own connectivity that the agent can reach the state the task asks about; an unreachable target silently turns into an impossible task rather than a hard one.
steps.accept: The reachability check succeeds from the instance's own connectivity for the state the task asks about.

steps.title: Parameterize and freeze
steps.detail: Expose the constraint values as parameters, sweep them to build the corpus, and record the seed and parameter set per instance so any instance can be regenerated exactly.
steps.accept: The seed and the parameter set are recorded, and re-running the generator with them reproduces the same instance.

curation_notes: Compare the corpus's segmentation and topology against the asset library's ground-truth labels where the library carries them, and report how many instances were generated and the spread of the structural parameters actually realised.
Sweep the constraint values to build the corpus, and confirm the corpus covers the declared structural variation instead of repeating one layout.
verifier: the generator script exits 0 and produces the requested number of instances with distinct parameter values
the validity checker reports zero collisions, zero out-of-bounds elements and zero constraint violations across the corpus
a reachability check succeeds for the task-relevant target state of every instance
segmentation or topology of generated instances matches the asset library's ground-truth labels
pitfalls: proposals without a geometry-compilation step look plausible but contain intersections or impossible placements
constraints kept as prose instead of costs leak into the corpus as violations
a generator with no seeded parameters produces a corpus that does not actually cover the declared variation

source_papers.title: SubTGraph: Large-Scale Subterranean Environment Synthesis with Controllable Topological Variability for Robotic Autonomy Validation
source_papers.note: builds a cost matrix from user-specified structural constraints to guide Dijkstra in procedurally generating multi-level worlds from a tile library, ships 150 worlds, and validates them against topometric ground truth

source_papers.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
source_papers.note: hierarchical sampler with diffusion priors for arrangements inside functional zones, then a compiler that uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction; the only compared method with no detected mesh collisions or out-of-bounds objects

source_papers.title: V-CAGE: Vision-Closed-Loop Agentic Generation Engine for Robotic Manipulation
source_papers.note: inpainting-guided scene construction arranges context-aware layouts, and unreachable target positions are identified as a primary cause of tasks failing prematurely

recipes.name: Skill-library exploration with verifier-guided search
recipes.summary: Expose the environment's capabilities as a few parameterised closed-loop skills, let an agent search over them under a verifier reporting partial progress, and distil the winning traces into reviewable scripts.
recipes.background: Rather than scripting the trajectory, expose the environment's capabilities as a library of reusable, parameterized, closed-loop skills and let a reasoning agent search over that library until it finds a verified path to the goal. Each skill takes parameters and returns an outcome; the agent invokes it, observes the result, and writes verification, reflection and memory to decide the next invocation, so the search is driven by evidence rather than by a predetermined execution pipeline. The library is what makes the approach scale: a small set of skills with expressive parameters serves thousands of instances, and the winning traces can be distilled into compact scripts. The property that must be preserved is closure - every skill reads the current state and acts on it, never replays an open-loop action sequence - because an open-loop skill turns the search into a no-op and produces traces that do not transfer.
recipes.produces: One verified trajectory over closed-loop skills, distilled into a compact script that reaches the goal state under the verifier.
when_to_use: the target exposes a set of capabilities rather than one fixed workflow
the goal is reachable but the correct sequence of capability calls is not known in advance
a reusable parameterized action space is preferred over a task-specific program
not_when_to_use: the correct procedure is a short fixed sequence that can be written down directly
the environment cannot report the outcome of a skill invocation
inputs: an environment exposing a capability or action API
a library of parameterized closed-loop skills implemented against that API
a verifier able to score partial as well as final goal states

steps.title: Extract the skill set from the source
steps.detail: Group the environment's primitive operations into a small set of reusable closed-loop skills with clear parameters (what to pick, where to place, what to query); prefer few expressive skills over many rigid ones.
steps.accept: Each skill has clear parameters and a stated effect, and the library stays small and expressive rather than many rigid skills.

steps.title: Make every skill closed-loop
steps.detail: Each skill reads current state, executes and returns an observation; reject open-loop replays of a fixed action list at review time, because they cannot support exploration and the traces they produce do not generalize.
steps.accept: Every skill reads the current state and returns an observation, and the library contains no open-loop action list.

steps.title: Implement a verifier for partial goals
steps.detail: Write the checker that reports how much of the goal is satisfied so the search gets signal before the goal is reached; a binary end-only check turns the search into blind retrying.
steps.accept: The verifier reports how much of the goal is satisfied, so a partial solution scores above nothing.

steps.title: Search with verification, reflection and memory
steps.detail: The agent invokes a skill, records the outcome, generates a verification and a reflection on what happened, keeps that in memory, and selects the next skill; expand alternatives at branches where verification failed.
steps.accept: The search records an outcome, a verification and a reflection for each invocation, and expands alternatives at branches where verification failed.

steps.title: Harvest and filter successful traces
steps.detail: Keep only traces that reach the goal under the verifier and whose steps satisfy the library's parameter constraints; discard traces that succeed by accident.
steps.accept: Every kept trace reaches the goal under the verifier, and every step is a declared skill called with in-range parameters.

steps.title: Distil into a reusable artifact
steps.detail: Compress the winning traces into a script or policy so each instance carries a compact reviewable solution, and leave the skill library unchanged so the same skills apply to new instances.
steps.accept: The winning trace is compressed into a script or policy that reaches the goal under the verifier, and the skill library is left unchanged.

curation_notes: Scale the run without losing determinism: decouple trajectory planning, execution and storage into asynchronous stages, balance load across workers and tolerate failures, so throughput rises while the corpus stays reproducible.
Record the exploration tree per instance - branches expanded, verification outcomes, search budget - so a run can be replayed and compared across instances.
verifier: a verifier script reports the goal state satisfied after the agent's final step
every step of the trace is a call to a declared skill with in-range parameters
the skill library contains no open-loop action list; each skill returns an observation
re-running the instance from the recorded seed reproduces the same goal state
pitfalls: open-loop skills make the search a no-op and produce traces that do not transfer
a verifier that only fires at the end leaves the search without guidance
one giant skill hides the decision the agent is supposed to make and inflates apparent success

source_papers.title: SkillWeaver: Agentic Exploration over Neural Interaction Skills for Scalable Robot Data Generation
source_papers.note: neural interaction skills as reusable parameterized closed-loop policies; a VLM agent invokes and parameterizes them, produces verification, reflection and memory, and organizes exploration as verifier-guided tree search across 14.1K scenes

source_papers.title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control
source_papers.note: language-model programs compose perception APIs and control primitives into feedback loops, with hierarchical code generation that recursively defines undefined functions

source_papers.title: Nimbus: A Unified Embodied Synthetic Data Generation Framework
source_papers.note: decoupled execution model separating trajectory planning, rendering and storage into asynchronous stages, with dynamic scheduling, global load balancing and fault tolerance for sustained generation throughput
